subject: OrbitPay — next steps on PO vs card and invoice requirements
message_1_subject: OrbitPay — next steps on PO vs card and invoice requirements
message_1_body:
Hi Helena / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking time earlier today — great discovery. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Procurement path: You mentioned procurement prefers a PO for new vendors but small pilot customers sometimes start on card. Please confirm which path OrbitPay is aiming for for the initial pilot (PO or card).
- Commercial docs: Our standard SOW + MSA are available; procurement asked about key commercial terms (net-30 options and tax handling). I’ve attached a short procurement checklist and a sample invoice (PDF).
- Invoice requirements: From our side, we can support invoice metadata fields (billing address, VAT/Tax ID, PO number) and send invoices to billing@orbitpay.com. Can you confirm preferred invoice delivery (email vs portal) and whether OrbitPay requires a specific PO number format?
- Marketplace interest: You mentioned evaluation of AWS Marketplace for procurement — if you want us to enable marketplace billing instead of vendor invoicing, we can loop in partnerships; that usually changes billing cadence and tax handling.

Next steps proposed: 
1) Helena, confirm PO vs card for the pilot and preferred invoice delivery method by EOD Monday (2025-07-14).
2) Procurement, if PO: send the required vendor registration form or a sample PO schema so our finance team can validate. If card: confirm cardholder email and limits.
3) Rishi/Marissa: we’ll produce the required vendor docs (W-9, sample invoice) and provide a short procurement pack.

Attachments: redwood-procurement-template.pdf (procurement checklist), sample_invoice-redwood.pdf, W9-Redwood.pdf

Thanks — I’ll hold on action until I hear your preference.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

message_2_subject: Re: OrbitPay — next steps on PO vs card and invoice requirements
message_2_body:
Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from my side: 

- Pilot procurement path: Procurement prefers to start with a PO for auditability. They may allow a temporary card for a quick POC but likely want PO for anything that looks like production.
- Invoice delivery: billing@orbitpay.com is correct; we prefer emailed PDF invoices with an attached CSV that includes line-level tax amounts.
- PO format: We use PO numbers that start with OP-YYYY-#### (e.g., OP-2025-0456). I’ll confirm if there are additional fields required (cost center, project code).
- Marketplace: We are evaluating AWS Marketplace, but that will take a few weeks — keep marketplace as an optional path for now.

Procurement (cc’d) — can you confirm whether OrbitPay will need vendor registration (tax forms/Vendor Portal) before issuing the initial PO? If so, what’s the best email to send the Redwood vendor packet to?

I’ll follow up once procurement confirms.

Thanks,
Helena Brooks
Director, Partnerships (BizOps)
OrbitPay
helenab@orbitpay.com
message_3_subject: Re: OrbitPay — next steps on PO vs card and invoice requirements
message_3_body:
Hi Rishi / Helena —

We will issue a PO for the pilot. Requirements from procurement: 
1) Vendor registration form (attached) + W-9 for US entities (or equivalent tax doc).
2) Invoices must include: Invoice number, Invoice date, PO number (OP- format), Line-item descriptions and unit prices, Tax/VAT where applicable, Billing address, Remit to address.
3) Net terms: We have a standard net-30 for new vendors but can discuss net-45 for strategic vendors.
4) Invoice delivery: Email to billing@orbitpay.com and please copy procurement@orbitpay.com on the first invoice.

Please send the completed vendor packet and W-9. Also include a sample invoice showing the PO number mapping.

Thanks,
OrbitPay Procurement
procurement@orbitpay.com

message_4_subject: Re: OrbitPay — vendor docs and sample invoice (attached)
message_4_body:
Thanks for the clear list — attaching the requested docs. Summary of what I’ve attached and next steps below: 

Attachments: redwood-procurement-template.pdf (completed vendor packet), W9-Redwood.pdf, sample_invoice-redwood.pdf

What we provided: 
- Completed vendor packet: includes Redwood legal name, tax ID/EIN, remit-to address, payment instructions.
- W-9: standard US tax form.
- Sample invoice: shows how PO number will be represented on the invoice (Invoice -> Line items -> Tax line -> Total), and a CSV export mapping line-level tax.

Redwood can accept PO-based billing and supports net-30 by default. If OrbitPay needs net-45, we can escalate to our finance lead — please flag that in your reply.

Regarding marketplace: if OrbitPay elects AWS Marketplace later, that will change the invoicing flow; we recommended waiting until procurement signs off.

Next actions: 
- Procurement: confirm receipt of attachments and whether any additional vendor attestations are required.
- Helena: once procurement confirms PO issuance, please share the first PO number and target billing date.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
